lines.text: In sixteen twenty-eight, the king of Sweden built the mightiest warship in the world.
It sank... before it even left the harbor.
Her name was the Vasa. Sixty-four guns. Main character energy.
But before she sailed, thirty men ran across her deck, to test how steady she was.
After three runs, she was rocking so hard, the admiral stopped the test.
His big move? He said he wished the king were home. That was the plan.
Tenth of August. The Vasa sets sail from Stockholm, flags out, full aura.
A small gust tips her over. Slowly... she comes back up.
Her lower gunports are wide open, and the sea pours straight in!
She sinks just thirteen hundred meters out. About thirty people die.
The problem? Too much weight, way too high. She was cooked from day one.
And after the inquiry? Nobody was punished. No cap.
She lay in the mud for three hundred and thirty-three years.
Then in nineteen sixty-one, they lifted her out, and today she's the best-preserved seventeenth-century ship on Earth.
Fumbled her very first trip... and still became a legend.
